## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

No issue found in the tested scope. **Verified:** filtering `window_rects()` on `.visible == true` removes covered siblings of a maximized or fullscreen window from every picker path that uses it, and the new test catches the old filter.

### Verified: covered windows are dropped, visible ones are kept

In Hyprland 0.56.2, `hyprctl clients -j` reports `visible` from `CWindow::visible()`, which requires `!hidden`, a mapped surface and nonzero combined alpha. When a workspace client is maximized or fullscreen, Hyprland fades the fullscreen alpha of other windows to 0. Pinned windows and a floating window focused above the maximized one are exempt. Covered siblings therefore end up `hidden: false, visible: false`, as the PR describes. Because `visible` implies `!hidden`, the new filter selects a subset of the old one and can only drop rectangles the compositor is not drawing.

Rectangles offered to slurp and window resolution, run against synthetic `hyprctl` JSON shaped after the Hyprland source (monitor `MON` is 1920x1080):

```text
scenario                              base (hidden != true)                     head (visible == true)
maximized tiled pair, windows mode    MON | 10,40 1900x1030 | 10,40 940x1030    MON | 10,40 1900x1030
fullscreen + pinned floating          MON | fullscreen | covered tiled |        MON | fullscreen | pinned
  + unfocused floating underneath       pinned | covered floating
tabbed group (inactive members        MON | 10,40 940x1030 | 970,40 940x1030   unchanged
  share one geometry)
--take-window, cursor over the        10,40 940x1030 (covered window)           10,40 1900x1030 (maximized)
  covered half
--select-window next                  warps to covered window centre            stays on maximized window
```

The PR's own test passes on the head and fails on the base (`60663faf`) at the maximized case. The `visible` key first appears in Hyprland 0.55.0, the same release that added the Lua config and `hyprctl eval` this head already depends on, so a stock install always provides it.

**Scope note:** `visible` is alpha-based, not a geometric occlusion check. A window completely covered by an ordinary (non-maximized) floating window still reports `visible: true` and is still offered, on both base and head. This matches the linked issue; only the PR title reads broader. Source reading also indicates that during the fade after a maximize or fullscreen toggle, covered windows briefly still report `visible: true`. That timing was not tested.

**Optional test improvement:** `fail "$description" "expected:\n$expected\nactual:\n$actual"` passes through `printf '%s\n'` in `base-test.sh`, so the `\n` separators print literally in the failure output (observed when running the test against the base). Using `$'\n'`, as `hyprland-keyboard-layout-test.sh` does, prints real line breaks.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the change against Hyprland 0.56.2 and slurp 1.5.0 source. The PR's test run in an isolated sandbox on head and base. Synthetic `hyprctl` JSON scenarios through `windows` mode, `--take-window` and `--select-window`, with stubbed `hyprctl`, `slurp` and `hyprpicker`. No live Hyprland session, so real picker UX and fade timing are untested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
